A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Video-MME and provide readable text, tables and figures. The main-text analyses can be matched to their revised or relocated counterparts, including v3's supplementary Sections 7–8. No material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 4–5, certificate-length measurements, modality analyses and qualitative model-error cases.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of an expanded model set, revised numerical results and modality analyses, including the supplemental subcategory results.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedure retains video collection, three four-option questions per video, independent annotation review and Gemini 1.5 Pro filtering of text-answerable questions. No new proposed model or algorithmic component is introduced; the substantive procedural revisions concern evaluation settings.

E1.justification: Both retain 900 videos and 2,700 questions covering six domains, 30 subcategories, 12 task types and the same duration bands and modality conditions. Additional reported subcategory results and revised associated-file counts do not introduce a new task, domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Gemini 1.5 Flash, ShareGPT4Video, VILA-1.5, VITA-1.0 and VITA-1.5. Figure 3 also replaces LLaVA-NeXT-Video with VILA-1.5 in the task-specific comparison. These changes substantially expand and revise the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Reported frame budgets change from 10 to 384 for GPT-4o and from 32 to 64 for Chat-UniVi-V1.5. Certificate-length sampling changes from five to three videos per class. v3 specifies timestamp-matched subtitles for all models, whereas v1 explicitly gives Gemini all subtitles; however, v3 retains conflicting 'complete subtitles' wording. Available subtitle/audio counts also change from 713/869 to 744/900.

E4.justification: Figure 4 extends the existing analysis of modality effects from 10 to all 30 subcategories within the supplied PDFs. The certificate-length analysis is revised, while the duration analysis and two qualitative error cases are retained; the latter are relocated to supplementary Section 8.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies and descriptive dataset statistics without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The certificate sample-size revision does not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 contain extensive numerical revisions: overall frame-only accuracy changes from 75.7% to 75.0% for Gemini and from 66.2% to 71.9% for GPT-4o. The leading open-source entry changes from LLaVA-NeXT-Video at 52.5% to newly evaluated VILA-1.5 at 59.0%. Dataset statistics and subcategory results also change. Revised settings prevent interpreting these as established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Both retain the same certificate-length definition: the summed duration of the minimum necessary and sufficient video subclips. Neither introduces new theorems, proofs, formal assumptions or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The four central benchmark contributions remain diversity, temporal coverage, multiple modalities and expert annotations. Both retain claims of applicability to image and video MLLMs, Gemini's leading performance, benefits from additional modalities and difficulty with longer videos. Updated headline numbers do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The audio-related applicability qualification changes: v1 says no evaluated open-source model supports audio, whereas v3 says most do not and explicitly notes omitted audio evaluation. The principal explanations involving harder questions, sparse frame sampling and long-context difficulty, together with the proposed future directions, remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section 7 newly specifies regular-expression answer extraction and frame counts for added models, and expands the subtitle-selection explanation. Most prompting and frame-extraction instructions were already disclosed in v1 Section 3.1 and are relocated or revised. The project-page link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to newer benchmarks including InfiniBench, MMBench-Video, LVBench and LongVideoBench, alongside works supporting newly evaluated models. It removes the VTimeLLM discussion and some earlier citations. These update the research context without substantially redefining Video-MME's positioning.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, detailed settings and qualitative model cases move into supplementary sections, and the conclusion is substantially compressed. Numerous body paragraphs and captions are rewritten, producing a substantial reorganization of the narrative despite largely retained scientific claims.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with extensive repositioning and resizing of tables and figures. Figure 4 expands from a 10-panel main-text display to a full-page, 30-panel supplemental figure. Table 4 gains model rows, and Figure 3 updates its comparator legend and caption.

improvement.justification: The broader model comparison and complete 30-subcategory modality breakdown make v3 more useful and allow more evidence to be inspected directly in the paper. Additional answer-extraction details modestly improve reproducibility. These gains are limited by conflicting subtitle instructions and a new error in Section 4.2: the stated 16.7-point multilingual audio gain belongs to subtitles in Table 5. The central benchmark design and analyses remain largely intact.
